objects.original: Author-derived canonical P: a finite real square-matrix field f, its genuine matrix-valued Bochner probability mean, and positive definiteness. Tropp supplies background, not a printed P theorem.
objects.reconstructed: The decoder reconstructs exactly a finite real matrix field, Bochner integral and symmetric positive-definite conclusion.
objects.evidence: P17-21 has Matrix ι ι ℝ, Integrable f μ, AE Matrix.PosDef and the actual integral. P25-48 keeps Hermiticity and proves strict quadratic tests. Raw Tropp pp8-9 does not print this standalone statement; current publication and reader disclose author-derived status. No complex-source generality is claimed.

domains.original: Arbitrary measurable outcome space with a probability law; any finite real matrix index, including the empty index; integrable f and AE-PD values.
domains.reconstructed: The decoder names the same probability/measurable setting and finite index, expressly allows an empty index, and interprets the integral as Bochner.
domains.evidence: P18-21 quantifies independent universes u,v, finite ι, measurable Ω and IsProbabilityMeasure μ. No Nonempty ι is added. Probability provides nonzero total mass for the scalar strictness argument; empty matrix indices have no nonzero test vector. The generic theorem does not assert positive trace for empty matrices.

quantifiers.original: For every such index, outcome space, probability measure and f, integrability and AE positive definiteness imply positive definiteness of the mean; every nonzero quadratic direction is tested separately.
quantifiers.reconstructed: The decoder reconstructs the same universal quantifiers and implication, with no common samplewise or directionwise lower bound.
quantifiers.evidence: P18-21 and P29 intro x hx fix an arbitrary nonzero x after the mean is chosen. The AE premise is used separately at that x; the proof does not assume simultaneous uniform positivity of the integrand over all directions.

assumptions.original: Finite real matrix carrier, measurable outcome space, probability law, genuine Bochner integrability and AE-PD are the natural generic P data, rather than premises added to the concrete Gaussian T.
assumptions.reconstructed: The decoder lists exactly these data; decidable equality and universe separation elaborate the finite type carrier.
assumptions.evidence: P18-21 has no additional bundled Prop, hidden global variable, source bound, spectral gap or nonempty-index premise. hf and hpos are used in the proof. T184-186 derives its P inputs internally. The source MGF existence caution is respected rather than replaced by a totalized nonintegrable integral.

conclusion.original: The true Bochner mean is positive definite: Hermitian and strictly positive quadratic form on every nonzero real vector.
conclusion.reconstructed: The decoder states exactly this, including symmetry and the empty-index vacuity.
conclusion.evidence: P25-28 obtains Hermiticity from the existing PSD-integral node. P35-46 obtains a strictly positive scalar integral, using integrability and contradiction with AE zero under probability. P47-48 commutes the continuous linear quadratic functional with the same integral. The result is PD, not merely PSD.

scopes.original: Canonical real integration infrastructure derived from background; no assertion of a printed Tropp P signature, full complex theorem, matrix-log identity, strict trace for empty carriers, or Bernstein theorem.
scopes.reconstructed: The reconstructed theorem has precisely the real Bochner-integral/PD scope and makes no extra analytic or concentration claim.
scopes.evidence: Whole P1-50 contains only this theorem and its proof. Current source attribution, reader assumptions and boundary explicitly separate the associated Gaussian application from P and disclose that neither standalone P nor the four-family bridge is printed. Tropp's non-strict expectation order is background, not falsely cited as the strictness proof.

constant_dependencies.original: No concentration constants, dimension prefactors, spectral lower bound or matrix-exponential parameter occur in generic P.
